changes.headline: The recovery faded on the inventory build, and the spread, not flat price, took the strain
changes.dek: Asia unwound Tuesday's recovery with WTI falling about twice as hard as Brent, the spread widening to a more than two-week high, and the industry inventory estimate printing well above consensus ahead of today's report. Brent Jan27 settled $93.14, up $0.70, and WTI Dec26 settled $86.01, up $0.29, on Tuesday (Reuters, Nov 17), and Asia gave the recovery back to Brent $92.53 and WTI $84.77 at 0550 GMT on Wednesday (Reuters, Nov 18). WTI fell roughly twice as hard as Brent and the Brent to WTI spread widened from $7.13 at the settle toward a more than two-week high. The industry estimate for the week ending Nov 13 printed crude up 5.28 million barrels and gasoline up 5.12 million against a survey consensus of 1.0 and 1.4 million. Brent's prompt spread is still backwardated at about $2.80, against more than $3 a month ago.
changes.balance_read: The surplus is moving from forecast to stock test: an industry build of 5.28 million barrels against a 1.0 million consensus is what today's report grades, while the basin balance keeps tanking toward December storage of 76.24 million barrels against 80.6 million of working capacity and the December apportionment notice stays unpublished.

changes.headline: A second strike on the Khasab vessel and a direct US and Iran exchange, on a week-old flow gauge
changes.dek: The Khasab vessel was reported struck a second time with one seafarer missing, and the US and Iran exchanged fire directly on Nov 17, while the latest measured clearance stays a week old. UKMTO Warning 208-26 was updated on Nov 17: a second strike and another fire were reported on the vessel attacked north of Khasab on Nov 16, with the crew unaccounted for. Indian authorities identified the vessel as the Panama-flagged LPG carrier Tara Gas, with subsequent Indian reporting of one seafarer missing and two injured. The IRGC said it targeted a US radar system in Bahrain on Nov 17, US fighter jets struck an IRGC missile launch site on Qeshm Island, and Bahrain intercepted further Iranian aerial attacks early on Nov 18. Iranian claims of six tankers struck since Sunday remain unconfirmed. Kpler's latest measured clearance, to Nov 11, is 8,264 kb/d, 48 percent of pre-war.
changes.balance_read: The confirmed tempo now carries a human cost and a direct US and Iran exchange of fire, but the measured flow gauge has not moved in a week; the strait's risk pricing stays live without a confirmed new barrel removed, and the flow print, not the incident count, is still what converts tempo into supply.
changes.publishers: UKMTO Warning 208-26 Update 001, Nov 17, 2026; Reuters, Nov 17 to 18, 2026; Kpler briefing, Nov 13, 2026

changes.headline: The front month is still a mark, the traded strip tightened again, and the notice is late
changes.dek: December WCS marked -$28.22 on zero lots for a ninth straight session while the traded deferred strip tightened a dollar on volume, and the December notice stayed unpublished after the nominations close. December WCS settled -$28.22 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 17) on zero lots, a ninth straight session without a December trade, with December outright at $57.79 on Tuesday's WTI settle. The traded strip tightened for a second day: Jan27 -$24.75, up $1.00 on 500 lots, Feb27 -$23.25 on 45 lots and Mar27 -$22.30, and January's ARV to TMW spread printed +$8.00. November apportionment stands at Light 19 percent and Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert. December nominations closed Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST and no December notice had been published as of this morning's check, so the registered December call of Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent remains ungraded.
changes.balance_read: December WCS remains a mark into an apportionment notice that has not published a day after the close that sets it; the traded deferred tightening says the winter strip is wide but not widening, and the notice is the next physical print on the front.
changes.publishers: ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 17, 2026; Enbridge notice, Oct 20, 2026

flags.title: December apportionment: the registered call is Light 14 and Heavy 9, and the notice is unpublished a day after the close
flags.detail: November Mainline apportionment (Light 19 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 7 percent at Kerrobert) is in effect. The registered December call is Light 14 percent and Heavy 9 percent. December nominations closed Tuesday Nov 17 at 0700 MST and the Enbridge notice that grades the call had not been published as of the Nov 18 morning check. The evidence pack includes the balance build with supply running about 200 kb/d a month above the proven 4,541.6 kb/d egress bound into tanks, a December front month that has not traded in nine sessions, and deferred strip tightening on volume for two straight days. Trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment notice, or a material change in the physical backdrop before it publishes

flags.title: Confirmed tempo is rising and the flow gauge is a week old: clearance 8,264 kb/d to Nov 11
flags.detail: Two tanker incidents are confirmed in the current cycle: the outbound vessel in Warning 207-26 on Nov 16, crew accounted for, and the vessel in Warning 208-26 north of Khasab, reported struck a second time on Nov 17 with one seafarer missing and two injured on Indian reporting. The US and Iran exchanged fire directly on Nov 17 and Bahrain intercepted further attacks early Nov 18. Iranian claims of six tankers struck since Sunday carry no named vessel and no confirmation. Kpler's latest measured clearance is 8,264 kb/d to Nov 11, 48 percent of pre-war, and is now a week old. A confirmed flow interruption reprices the strait; continued incidents at the current measured clearance keep the surplus in charge. Trigger: A fresh measured clearance print materially below 8,264 kb/d, or confirmation of a loadings halt from a tracker, owner or UKMTO product

flags.title: Inventory test today: industry build of 5.28 million against a 1.0 million consensus
flags.detail: The industry estimate for the week ending Nov 13 printed crude up 5.28 million barrels and gasoline up 5.12 million, against a Wall Street Journal and Dow Jones survey consensus of crude up 1.0 million and gasoline up 1.4 million. The official report lands Nov 18 at 10:30 a.m. ET. The industry estimate has had the direction right four straight weeks while the official report confirmed only a fraction of its magnitude in each of the last two. A confirmed build near the industry estimate turns the surplus from a forecast into a stock level; a draw against both estimates reopens the pricing. Trigger: The EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending Nov 13, released Nov 18 at 10:30 a.m. ET

forward_calendar.what: EIA report for week ending Nov 13, and Irving Osprey resumption date
forward_calendar.detail: The inventory report for the week ending Nov 13 is the first inventory test of the surplus pricing, with the industry estimate at a 5.28 million barrel crude build against a survey consensus of 1.0 million. The last dated outage in the window is scheduled to resume operations the same day.
The December WTI contract expires Friday, which puts the front differential's first trade, whenever it comes, inside the expiry week for a second straight month.
